answer.rationale: Rated against the specific standard of sustainable, long-term, QUALIFIED revenue, not against generic 'did the metric move.' memory_57 (4) and memory_44 (4) are the only two that name revenue/pipeline quality and gesture at durability — 57 explicitly checked retention, 44 speaks to pipeline quality rather than raw volume — though both omit time horizon, sample, and whether 'qualified' was defined consistently. memory_31 (3) claims a 'durable' lift, which is the only durability language in the set, but activation is two or three steps upstream of revenue and no revenue link is asserted. memory_86 (2) and memory_91 (2) report funnel and engagement proxies only (completion, time-to-value, week-one engagement); neither says whether those accounts ever converted, expanded, or stayed, so they are weak evidence for the objective even if they are true. memory_73 is rated 1 and is the least supported: it is the memory most likely to be acted on this week given the competitor's entry pricing, and it is precisely the memory whose omissions matter most. It reports 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' but says nothing about margin, discount depth, renewal at list price, or churn of promo-acquired cohorts — the exact variables that separate sustainable qualified revenue from pulled-forward, low-quality revenue. Discount-acquired SMB accounts are the canonical case where acquisition and short-run revenue rise while lifetime value falls, and unlike memory_57 this memory does not claim any retention check was run. It is also the oldest-context claim being applied to a materially changed market: it was consolidated on day 31 in the absence of a price war, and matching a competitor's entry pricing today is a different intervention than the one that was tested. High apparent strength, near-zero evidence on the 'sustainable' half of the objective, and maximum pull on this cycle's single slot is the worst combination in the set. Practical note for the experiment decision: the current declines are in activation (-6%) and onboarding completion (-4%), and the memories touching those surfaces (31, 86, 91) are the ones rated weakest on revenue linkage — so whichever is chosen should be instrumented to downstream qualified revenue and retention, not just to the funnel metric it is expected to move.
